name: TDG Grade Gate
rule: MAY ONLY SHRINK. A run reporting more than `ceiling` is a regression and fails. Lowering this number is the only permitted edit.
why: Measured identical on origin/main and on release/1.16.0, so this release introduces zero new debt.
All 61 are grade [B] with complexity 13-15, spread across unrelated subsystems (parser/includes, resolver, state, prove, mcp, cli/lsp).
Refactoring them is its own project, not a rider on a bug-fix release. Holding fixes hostage to unrelated debt is how a gate trains people to bypass it.
The pre-commit TDG hook already enforces no-regression per commit, so this ratchet formalises what is already true rather than adding a new constraint.
not_a_bypass: The gate still reports CB-200 as failing against grade A. This records the number so it cannot silently grow, per the dogfood protocol: 'Record a dated baseline in the crate rather than weakening a gate.'
